candidates.source_summary: Plans for a direct rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.
candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times

candidates.source_summary: RBH has submitted an outline planning application for up to 270 homes for affordable or social rent in Lower Falinge, Rochdale. The proposals also include demolishing seven remaining blocks.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: RBH has submitted an outline planning application for up to 270 homes for affordable or social rent in Lower Falinge, Rochdale. The proposals also include demolishing seven remaining blocks. The application covers two sites, on land near Redcross Street and next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road. RBH said the proposed mix of apartments and family homes would increase the number of bed spaces in the community by more than 300. The housing provider said the seven blocks proposed for demolition were at the end of their life and would no longer be able to provide safe, warm homes. The plans also include landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets and new walking routes. RBH said the homes would be designed to meet the Future Homes Standard, with measures intended to reduce energy use and heating costs. They would also be accessible and adaptable to residents’ changing needs. Hannah Fleming, RBH director of regeneration and asset improvement, said residents, businesses, community groups and local stakeholders had been consulted before the application was submitted. She said, “Our aim is to build new homes that current and future customers will be proud to live in and strengthen the bonds that already exist within the local community in Lower Falinge and Rochdale town centre.

candidates.source_summary: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants. Today marked the end of a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester after Hopwood DePree took legal action against the council which ended an exclusivity agreement to sell the historic Grade II-listed hall to him. Following the decision, Mr DePree said: “This is of course incredibly disappointing and a huge blow to our community, our supporters around the world, as well as the UK’s charitable heritage rescue groups in general. “However, please know that my team and I are already determining our legal options and next steps. “We will be watching closely to keep an eye on Rochdale Borough Council’s efforts to save Hopwood Hall for the community, and restore it to its former glory.” Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. READ MORE:Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 Finalists Announced

candidates.source_summary: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_summary: The battle for Hopwood Hall returns to the courtroom today with ownership of the historic manor house at stake.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The battle for Hopwood Hall returns to the courtroom today with ownership of the historic manor house at stake. Hopwood DePree and Rochdale Council begin a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester later over Mr DePree’s bid to restore his ancestral home. Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. The legal action initiated by Mr DePree was launched after he spent seven years working with the council to carry out vital repairs on the dilapidated site with a view to purchasing it. In November, 2024, the council ended its exclusivity agreement with Mr DePree, and said it would explore other options because no “commercially viable” business model had been presented. candidates.source_summary: A 15-year-old girl is facing charges after Regina police seized a BB handgun during an investigation involving two female youths.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A 15-year-old girl is facing charges after Regina police seized a BB handgun while investigating a weapons call. Police were called to the 5200 block on Rochdale Boulevard a 6 p.m. on Oct. 17, after receiving a report that three females were in possession of what appeared to be a firearm. According to a news release, officers arrived within minutes and located two girls matching the suspect description in the 4400 block of Rochdale Boulevard. During a search, police found a BB handgun in the waistband of one of the girls. Police later determined the second girl was in possession of the BB handgun during the incident, according to RPS. Police say the youth became uncooperative as officers attempted to arrest her and kicked an officer in the leg. She was taken into custody and the officer sustained minor injuries. The 15-year-old, who cannot be named under the Youth Criminal Justice Act, is charged with possession of a weapon, assaulting a peace officer and failure to comply with a disposition. She will make her first appearance in Regina Provincial Youth Court on Nov. 26.

candidates.source_summary: Fundraisers spent a night outdoors to raise awareness and vital funds for people experiencing homelessness in the community.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fundraisers spent a night outdoors to raise awareness and vital funds for people experiencing homelessness in the community. Supporters from across the borough came together at Rochdale’s Crown Oil Arena for the second Petrus Communities and RAFC Community Trust annual Sleep Out. Money raised will again go towards helping people through Changing Lives — a football initiative designed to support people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation. The programme aims to improve participants’ mental health, physical well-being, and social inclusion through free, inclusive football sessions. It also provides personal development opportunities, including pathways into volunteering, education, and employment. Louise Scriven, Fundraising and Partnerships Coordinator at Petrus, said: “The Sleep Out isn’t about pretending to experience homelessness. candidates.source_summary: Lee Bell salutes record-breaking Crewe after victory over Rochdale The Impartial Reporter
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Lee Bell was in jubilant mood after Crewe’s 3-2 success over Rochdale set a record-breaking start to a league campaign. Matus Holicek’s thumping finish and a double from Jordan Gibson was enough to stave off a second-half fightback from Dale and leave Crewe unbeaten in the first 11 games this term. Bell said: “It’s a big achievement with the club being 150 years old (in 2027) and for my players and staff to hold that record outright. “That’s what it takes to win a game in this league as Rochdale were on a run of five games unbeaten and played some good football, although I didn’t think they threatened us with that. “But when you’re 3-0 at home you do want it to be more comfortable than it was. They brought their big No 9 on (Emmanuel Dieseruvwe) and it was hard to contain them. “However, I thought there were plenty of opportunities for us to score a couple more goals which is what we have got to do. I want us to be an attacking side who play on the front foot most of the time. “Our second goal was really terrific. Owen Lunt is a beast and he floored their lad fairly to set up Jordan, which is exactly what we needed.” Crewe struck twice inside six minutes with first Holicek picking the ball up from Gibson and unleashing a drive from outside the box, which goalkeeper Sam Waller got a hand to, after 39 minutes.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A retired civil servant will be keeping extra warm this winter after winning 500 litres of heating oil. Liz Shrewsbury, who lives in a hamlet just outside Rochdale, won the prize in Craggs Energy’s Cosy Heating Club quarterly oil draw. However, I’d completely missed that as a Direct Debit customer, I’d been automatically entered into the Cosy Heating Club quarterly prize draw. So, that was a great surprise! “Now that I know, I’ve been sharing that fact with all my neighbours that use heating oil, as the entire hamlet is off-grid. “I was due to order a tank refill, so the call came at the perfect time. The money saved will help balance out increased transport fuel prices and rising day-to-day living costs, all of which seem to have been escalating so much in the last year.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Jordan Gibson netted twice as unbeaten Crewe registered a third consecutive victory with a 3-2 success over Rochdale. Matus Holicek fired the Alex ahead with a stunning strike before Gibson scored either side of the interval. A Joel Tabiner own goal and a late header from Aden Flint saw Dale cut the arrears, but the visitors went down to their first league defeat in six games. Crewe struck twice inside six minutes with first Holicek picking the ball up from Gibson and unleashing a drive from outside the box, which goalkeeper Sam Waller got a hand to, after 39 minutes. Young Chelsea loanee Kaiden Wilson was then brushed aside too easily by Owen Lunt and the midfielder squared the ball across the box for Gibson to tap in on the stroke of half-time before the latter poked in from 10 yards 10 minutes into the second half. Dale cut the arrears when Glenn Middleton’s cross diverted off Tabiner in the 65th minute and Flint headed in substitute Ed Francis’ cross from close range in the closing stages.

candidates.source_summary: After a turbulent two years of battling over Hopwood Hall, Rochdale’s council leader says the ‘cherished’ historic building will be brought back into use.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: After a turbulent two years of battling over Hopwood Hall, Rochdale’s council leader says the ‘cherished’ historic building will be brought back into use. Council bosses were quizzed over the future of the Middleton site following a High Court battle where the town hall prevailed against Hopwood DePree. The two day trial in Manchester Civil Justice Centre ruled that the council was not acting unlawfully when it ended an exclusivity agreement with the American filmmaker. Mr DePree entered an option agreement with the council to restore the hall back in 2017, until that agreement was ended in October 2024. Since then, Mr DePree, who claims ancestral connections with the 1400s stately home, has felt he had a legally binding agreement to purchase Hopwood Hall for £1. The High Court found that the ‘change of use’ planning approval was granted in 2022 wasn’t enough to trigger the option to purchase the hall for a ‘peppercorn fee’ – £1. In the first town hall meeting since the trial last month, council leader Neil Emmott was asked what the next steps were for the hall. Coun Emmott did not clarify a specific use for the future of the hall, but vowed to bring it back into use for the wider community. The council boss told the chamber on October 15 how his ‘door is always open’ to Hopwood DePree. Coun Emmott said if Mr DePree came back with a viable plan for the future of Hopwood Hall, the council would listen. In response to Coun Steve Potter’s question about the next steps for Hopwood Hall, Coun Emmott said: “The High Court’s judgment in relation to Hopwood Hall does not necessarily mark the end of the legal process. “Mr DePree has the right to seek permission to appeal the decision. The court has directed that any application for permission to appeal must be lodged by November 18, 2026, although there is scope for this deadline to be extended to November 28, 2026.
candidates.source_title: Hopwood Hall ‘will be brought back into community use’

candidates.source_summary: Is the future of the local pub in danger? That’s the fear in Littleborough where the closure of another pub has sparked outcry.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Is the future of the local pub in danger? That’s the fear in Littleborough where the closure of another pub has sparked outcry. A few months ago The Wheatsheaf closed down in the Rochdalian town. There is strong community interest in reopening the pub as a local asset, but a small loophole means they fear they can’t do that. When breweries or large companies that own and operate pubs sell on the building, they can include a covenant that prevents it from being re-used as a pub. This covenant is inserted into a sale to stop competitors taking the pub on the cheap, the latest town hall meeting was told. Coun Richard Jackson brought forward a motion to Rochdale council to address this very issue to reduce the continued loss of pubs in communities. The Littleborough Lakeside councillor told the chamber on October 15: “The reality is that around 50 per cent of pubs are owned by breweries or large pub companies. They have a history of damaging the industry as a whole. This often leads to tenant attrition. “We are acutely aware of pubs being closed down after numerous tenants have left the building. The point of this motion is to address the churn. “We have seen this at the former Royal Oak pub. This was sold with an anti-competition covenant.” The former Royal Oak pub was closed down in 2015 and then sold off and became a vape shop, which was later shut down by Trading Standards.
candidates.source_title: Town hall fears for the future of pubs

candidates.source_summary: Bonfire night is set to go off with a bang in Rochdale with a week full of events on offer.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Bonfire night is set to go off with a bang in Rochdale with a week full of events on offer. Yet again the council is putting on three firework display events in Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton – completely free of charge. Just like last year, Bowlee Community Park, Queens Park Road and Cronkeyshaw Common will all be dazzled by pyrotechnics. This year Rochdale council are trialling reduced noise firework displays to make the events more accessible to all. Festivities will begin on Monday, November 2 at Bowlee Community Park in Middleton. The next day (October 3) will be Heywood’s Queen’s Park Road event followed by the Cronkeyshaw Common event in Syke on October 4. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future A historic Manchester pub that has drawn visitors from around the world is fearing for its future amid plans for a large tower to be built nearby. The Marble Arch has been serving pints on Rochdale Road since 1888 when Queen Victoria sat on the throne and the city was rapidly industrialising. Plans by the McGoff Group to build a 17-storey tower with 153 flats next to the Grade II-listed pub have prompted concerns about the visual impact and the pub's continued existence. Manchester City Council said it accepted "some visual harm" would be caused as a result of the building going up, but would be "outweighed by the substantial public and regeneration benefits that the proposal would deliver". candidates.source_summary: The people who helped bring Rochdale’s historic Broadfield Park Slopes back to life were celebrated at a special event at Rochdale Town Hall.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The people who helped bring Rochdale’s historic Broadfield Park Slopes back to life were celebrated at a special event at Rochdale Town Hall. The celebration, arranged by Polly Brant, Rochdale Council Cultural Engagement officer, brought together volunteers, partners and people who have been involved in the project to recognise what has been achieved and, importantly, the contribution local people have made along the way. Guests watched a series of films created by Rochdale filmmaker Jack Grindrod and Breaking Barriers, capturing the people, stories, heritage and community involvement behind the transformation. The evening also featured poetry readings from Alende Amisi, a poet who grew up in Rochdale and was a young poet in residence during Rochdale’s Town of Culture. Passionate about the town and its heritage, Alende brought a personal perspective to an evening which was as much about Rochdale’s people as its history. A special thank you was also given to the many volunteers who have supported the project, giving their time to archaeological digs, activities and events and helping uncover and share the history of this important part of the town. The Grade II listed Broadfield Park Slopes sit between Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church and have been restored through a project delivered by Rochdale Development Agency working with Rochdale Borough Council, with funding from The National Lottery Heritage Fund. The work has restored the historic Packer Spout Fountain, created a new accessible pathway, improved landscaping, lighting and CCTV, and introduced new heritage interpretation. The lower lawn has also been terraced, creating a natural amphitheatre and new space for activities and events.

candidates.source_summary: St Cuthbert's Roman Catholic High School in Rochdale was evacuated today (October 16) after a 'bomb threat' was received in a call to the school
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Students have been evacuated after a high school in Rochdale was placed in lockdown following a 'bomb threat'. Pupils and staff at St Cuthbert’s RC High School were told to leave after the school received a communication indicating a possible bomb threat, according to St Teresa of Calcutta Catholic Academy Trust, which manages the school. Greater Manchester Police attended, and all school buildings were evacuated as a 'precautionary measure'. A spokesperson for St Teresa of Calcutta Catholic Academy Trust said: "All children and staff are safe and accounted for, in line with our established procedures. "Greater Manchester Police attended and parents and carers were notified immediately that their children had been removed to a safe distance and there was no threat or danger to anyone present. "We would like to assure everyone within the St Cuthbert’s School community that the safety and wellbeing of our children remains our absolute priority. "Specialist security operatives will conduct a full sweep of the building this afternoon to confirm if any further actions are required." The trust said that the school is expected to 'be open as normal' on Monday (October 19).
